points.t: A patient on (or recently stopped) pembrolizumab, nivolumab, ipilimumab or dabrafenib + trametinib with any new symptom.
Checkpoint inhibitors release T-cell brakes, so autoimmune inflammation can hit any organ, even months after stopping.
Ask ‘are you on cancer treatment?’; contact the 24-hour acute oncology hotline rather than treating alone; check interactions (dabrafenib lowers hormonal contraceptive levels).
Colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, myocarditis, hypophysitis/adrenal crisis, new type 1 diabetes/DKA, SJS/TEN.

items.t: Diarrhoea, breathlessness, severe headache, chest pain or new thirst/polyuria in a patient on immunotherapy: **same-day acute oncology** contact.
Fever on dabrafenib + trametinib: follow the protocol (interrupt) and contact the oncology team.

pearls.t: Explain that side-effects can be serious but are usually treatable *if caught early*: "ring the hotline, not the GP's routine line".
Vitiligo during anti-PD-1 therapy is common and often correlates with better response. Protect the depigmented skin from sun.
